Synoptic Arctic Survey 2021 - metatranscriptomics

Author

geweaa

Published

December 20, 2024

The raw data was procesesd using nf-core/metatdenovo (v1.0.1): https://nf-co.re/metatdenovo/1.0.1/ The following command was used to start the pipeline: nextflow run nf-core/metatdenovo -r dev -profile uppmax -params-file params.yaml The file params.yaml contained the following relevant parameters: skip_kofamscan: TRUE orf_caller: ‘prokka’ eukulele_db: ‘gtdb-r220’ input: ‘input.csv’ project: naiss2024-22-406

Apart from this, the pipeline was run on default parameters. GTDB release 220 was used for taxonomic annotation.

tpm <- read_tsv("data/megahit.prokka.counts.tsv.gz", show_col_types = F) %>% 
  select(orf, sample, count, tpm) %>%
  mutate(sample = gsub("R", ".", sample)) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c(
    "S1.1", "S1.2", "S2.1", "S2.2", "S3.1", "S3.2", "S4.1", "S4.2", "S5.1", "S6.1", 
    "S5.2", "S6.2", "S7.1", "S7.2", "S8.1", "S8.2", "S9.1", "S9.2", "S10.1", "S10.2"
  )))

meta <- read_tsv("data/sample_key.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  mutate(station = as.character(station)) %>%
  mutate(sample = gsub("R", ".", sample)) %>%
  select(-`user id`, -`>=q30(%)`) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = c(
    "S1.1", "S1.2", "S2.1", "S2.2", "S3.1", "S3.2", "S4.1", "S4.2", "S5.1", "S6.1", 
    "S5.2", "S6.2", "S7.1", "S7.2", "S8.1", "S8.2", "S9.1", "S9.2", "S10.1", "S10.2"
  ))) %>%
  mutate(depth = factor(depth, levels = c("10m", "chlMax")))

In total, there are 20 metatranscriptomes from five stations. At every station, samples were taken in duplicates from 10 m depth and from chl. max. On average, each sample has 81.2 million reads (sd 8.7, n = 20). Off all the transcripts, 53.0 % was functionally annotated (Eggnog mapper), 36.5 % was functionally annotated including a KO reference, 45.7 % of the transcripts was annotated on phylum level, 45.7 % on order level, 44.8 % on genus level, and 32.7 % on species level.

25.2 % of the transcript were functionally annotated with Prokka. A summary of the bioinformatic pipeline will soon be added to this introduction.

t <- tpm %>%

Community composition - phylum

Figure 4 explores the data by plotting the most abundant phyla over all samples, regardless if the RNA transcript was functionally annotated or not. Note that the taxonomy is outdated and needs to be updated (e.g. Pseudomonadota instead of Proteobacteria). 87.7 % of the annotated ORFs are affiliated with bacteria, while 13.1 % is affiliated with Archaea.

Beta diversity using NMDS (all stations)

As the metatranscriptomes from station 5 seem off (especially the duplicates), the ordination is run with (a) and without (b) this station. On a first glance it seems that the samples from 10 m depth and chlorophyll max. have been mixed up. The NMDS is run with default parameters.

Expand code 
set.seed(999)

nmds <- tpm %>%
  # Sum the abundance of both coverage per metagenome
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "orf") %>%
  # Filter out NA and add multiple KOs on new line
  filter(kegg_module != "-") %>% separate_rows(kegg_module, sep = ",") %>%
  # Sum the abundance of each KO within the metagenomes
  group_by(sample, kegg_module) %>% 
  summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot to prepare a numerical matrix
  pivot_wider(names_from = "kegg_module", values_from = "tpm", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample") %>%
  vegan::metaMDS()

nmds
Expand code 
nmds.scores <- vegan::scores(nmds)$sites %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample")
Expand code 
p1 <- nmds.scores %>%
  inner_join(meta, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(station = factor(station, levels = names(cols.station))) %>%
  # Plot

             y = NMDS2, 
             colour = station,
             shape = depth

  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 'dotted', linewidth = 0.25) +

  scale_shape_discrete(labels = c("10 m", "Chl. max"), name = "") +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols.station, name = "Station") +
  theme_tidy() +
  annotate('text', x = -Inf, y = -Inf, size = 7/.pt,
           label = paste('Stress = ', round(nmds$stress, digits = 2)),

  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin()),
    panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 0.75, colour = "black", fill = NA),
    legend.text = element_text(margin = margin(l = 0)),
    legend.box.margin = margin(l = -8)
    )

Beta diversity using NMDS (without station 5)

In this NMDS, the replicates from station 5 (S1 and S2) are removed prior to running the NMDS.

Expand code 
set.seed(555)

nmds <- tpm %>%
  filter(!sample %in% c("S1.1", "S1.2", "S2.1", "S2.2")) %>%
  # Sum the abundance of both coverage per metagenome
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "orf") %>%
  # Filter out NA and add multiple KOs on new line
  filter(kegg_module != "-") %>% separate_rows(kegg_module, sep = ",") %>%
  # Sum the abundance of each KO within the metagenomes
  group_by(sample, kegg_module) %>% 
  summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot to prepare a numerical matrix
  pivot_wider(names_from = "kegg_module", values_from = "tpm", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample") %>%
  vegan::metaMDS()

The gene list is from Royo-Llonch et al. [1]. It contains the KEGG ortholog (KO) and the pathway the gene is involved in. KOs of interest in the data that are not represented in the gene list are manually categorized. Shows the RNA transcripts for the carbon fixation pathways for each depth layer. To do so, one KO catalyzing the rate-limiting reaction was selected for each pathway. The Wood-Ljungdahl pathway was also included in this analysis but the representing KO was not detected, or the detected KO did not have a taxonomic annotation.

Expand code 
cols.order <- c( # Sorted on abundance
  "Rhizobiales_B" = "#D69C4E",
  "Streptomycetales" = "#972D15",
  "Rhodobacterales" = "#D8B70A",
  "PS1" = "#FAEFD1",
  "Pseudomonadales" = "#C7B19C",
  "Burkholderiales" = "#D5D5D3",
  "SAR86" = "#1B5331",
  "Nitrososphaerales" = "#A2A475",
  "Cyanobacteria" = "#00A08A",
  "Other" = "#046C9A"
)

 kos <- eggnog %>% 
  mutate(pathway = case_when(
    # C fixation
    kegg_ko == "K01601" ~ "Calvin cycle", # ribulose-bisphosphate carboxylase large chain - EC:4.1.1.39 - Calvin cycle
    kegg_ko == "K09709" ~ "3-hydroxypropionate bi-cycle", # 3-methylfumaryl-CoA hydratase - EC:4.2.1.153 - 3-hydroxypropionate bi-cycle
    kegg_ko == "K15019" ~ "HP/HB cycle", # 3-hydroxypropionyl-coenzyme A dehydratase - EC:4.2.1.116 - HP/HB cycle
    kegg_ko == "K00175" ~ "Reverse TCA cycle", # 2-oxoglutarate/2-oxoacid ferredoxin oxidoreductase subunit beta - EC:1.2.7.3 1.2.7.11 - Reverse TCA cycle
    kegg_ko == "K14534" ~ "DC/HB cycle", # 4-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydratase / vinylacetyl-CoA-Delta-isomerase - EC:4.2.1.120 5.3.3.3 - DC/HB cycle
    kegg_ko == "K00198" ~ "Wood-Ljungdahl pathway",  # anaerobic carbon-monoxide dehydrogenase catalytic subunit - EC:1.2.7.4 - Wood-Ljungdahl
    # N metabolism
    kegg_ko %in% c("K00368","K15864","K04561","K02305","K00376","K15877") ~ "Denitrification",
    kegg_ko %in% c("K10535","PF01774","PF00449","K00370") ~ "Nitrification",
    kegg_ko %in% c("K17877","K00366","K10534","K00367","K00360","K00372") ~ "Assimilatory nitrate reduction",
    kegg_ko %in% c("K00362","K00363","K03385","K15876") ~ "Dissimilatory nitrite reduction",
    kegg_ko %in% c("K10944","K10945","K10946") ~ "Ammonia monooxygenase (AmoABC)",
    kegg_ko == "K03320" ~ "Ammonium transporter (amt)",
    kegg_ko %in% c("K02586","K02588","K02591") ~ "Nitrogen fixation (nifDHK)",
    # Central C
    kegg_ko == "K01637" ~ "Glyoxylate cycle: ICL",
    kegg_ko == "K13937" ~ "Pentose phosphate pathway: G6PD",
    kegg_ko == "K00850" ~ "Glycolysis: PFK",
    kegg_ko == "K01690" ~ "ED pathway: edd",
    kegg_ko == "K00031" ~ "Citric acid cycle: icd",
    kegg_ko == "K18981" ~ "Uronate pathway: udh",
    kegg_ko == "K00948" ~ "PRPP biosynthesis: RPPK",    
    # Photosystems
    kegg_ko == "K02712" ~ "Photosystem II (psbK)",
    kegg_ko == "K02707" ~ "Photosystem II (psbE)",
    kegg_ko == "K02697" ~ "Photosystem I (psaJ)",
    kegg_ko == "K02274" ~ "Cytochrome c oxidase (coxA)",
    kegg_ko == "K02256" ~ "Cytochrome c oxidase (Cox1)",
    .default = NA
  )) %>% filter(!is.na(pathway)) %>%
  mutate(metabolism = case_when(
    kegg_ko %in% c("K01601","K09709","K15019","K00175","K14534","K00198") ~ "cfix",
    kegg_ko %in% c("K01637","K13937","K00850","K01690","K00031","K18981","K00948") ~ "c",
    kegg_ko %in% c("K02712","K02707","K02697","K02274","K02256") ~ "photo",
    .default = "n"
  )) %>%
  inner_join(tax, by = "orf") %>% inner_join(tpm, by = "orf", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  mutate(order = if_else(phylum == "Cyanobacteria", true = "Cyanobacteria", false = order)) %>%
  inner_join(meta, by = "sample") %>%
  mutate(order = if_else(order %in% names(cols.order),
                         order, "Other")) %>%
  group_by(pathway, metabolism, depth, order) %>% summarise(tpm = sum(tpm), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(order = factor(order, levels = names(cols.order)))

Figure 10 shows the tpm for each representative KO summed over all the samples (n = 20). N transformation, central C metabolism, and photosynthesis plus aerobic respiration. Udh uronate dehydrogenase, edd phosphogluconate dehydratase, icd isocitrate dehydrogenase, ICL isocitrate lyase, G6PD glucose-6-phosphate 1-dehydrogenase, PRPP phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate, RPPK ribose-phosphate pyrophosphokinase, ED: Entner–Doudoroff. Note how the transcripts involved in carbon fixation are predominantly represented by the Streptomycetales (Streptomyces sp.) and the Burkholderiales (Nitrosomonas sp.) while only few transcripts were detected affiliated with cyanobacteria. The oxidation from ammonia to nitrite (nitrification) is performed by Nitrosopumilus sp. while the further oxidation from nitrite to nitrate (K00370) is done by a representative from the family Nitrospinaceae.

Differential gene expression using edgeR

This analysis helps to identify differentially expressed genes between the 10 m depth and the chlorophyll max depth. Station 5 is not included in the analysis as it introduces too much noise.

Expand code 
library(edgeR)
i <- meta %>% filter(!station %in% c("5", "56")) %>% pull(sample)

m <- tpm %>%
  filter(sample %in% i) %>% # Leave out station 5 for the moment
  select(-tpm) %>%
  arrange(sample) %>%
  pivot_wider(values_from = "count", names_from = "sample", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("orf") # Create a numeric matrix

dge <- tpm %>%
  filter(sample %in% i) %>% # Leave out station 5 for the moment
  select(-tpm) %>%
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "orf") %>% separate_longer_delim(kegg_ko, delim = ",") %>%
  group_by(sample, kegg_ko) %>% summarise(count = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(kegg_ko != "-") %>%
  arrange(sample) %>%
  pivot_wider(values_from = "count", names_from = "sample", values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("kegg_ko") %>%
  DGEList(group = meta %>% filter(sample %in% i) %>% pull(depth), lib.size = colSums(m))

The chunk below is to create the design matrix, make the contract, and run the actual analysis using the functions glmQLfit() and glmQLFTest()

Expand code 
design.mat <- model.matrix(~ 0 + meta %>% filter(sample %in% i) %>% arrange(sample) %>% pull(depth))
rownames(design.mat) <- colnames(m)
colnames(design.mat) <- c("shallow", "deep")
contrast <- makeContrasts(depth = shallow-deep, levels = design.mat)

dge <- dge %>%
  calcNormFactors() %>%
  estimateDisp(design.mat) %>%
  glmQLFit(design.mat, robust = TRUE)

qlf <- glmQLFTest(dge, contrast = contrast)

The p-values are adjusted according to the false discovery rate, and the DE genes are joined with the functional and taxonomic annotation.

Expand code 
de <- topTags(qlf, adjust.method = "fdr", n = Inf) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("kegg_ko") %>% rename_with(tolower) %>%
  mutate(expression = case_when(
    fdr < 0.05 & logfc > 0 ~ "up",
    fdr < 0.05 & logfc < 0 ~ "down",
    .default = "non-de"
  )) %>%
  inner_join(eggnog, by = "kegg_ko") %>%
  inner_join(tax, by = "orf") %>% inner_join(tpm, by = "orf") %>%
  filter(expression != "non-de") %>% tibble()

remove(m, dge, qlf, contrast, design.mat)

As the contrast was shallow vs deep, upregulated means significantly higher in the shallow samples while downregulated means higher in the deeper samples. There are 439 KOs up regulated and 831 KOs down regulated. 0 KOs were not differential expressed.

The 25 KOs with the lowest (up in deeper samples) and 25 with the highest log fold-change are selected. Six of these KOs are represented in the gene list, the other 19 will be manually categorized. The number of 25 was arbitrary chosen. Many of these KOs are affiliated with the archaeon Nitrosopumilus that oxidizes ammonium and is capable of autotrophic growth using the hydroxypropionate/hydroxybutyrate cycle that is more energy efficient than other aerobic C fixation pathways, including the Calvin cycle (source: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1402028111). The fact that C fixation KOs affiliated with this genus are abundantly detected strongly suggests autotrophic growth, possibly due to a low concentration of organic carbon.

  mutate(order = if_else(

  mutate(order = factor(order, levels = names(cols.order))) %>%
  mutate(kegg_ko = paste(kegg_ko, pathway, sep = ": ")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = logfc,

seqtab <- read_tsv("data/amplicons/ASV_table.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(-1, names_to = "sample", values_to = "count") %>%
  filter(count > 0) %>%
  rename(seqid = ASV_ID) %>%
  group_by(sample) %>% mutate(relab = count / sum(count)) %>% ungroup()
  
asv <- read_tsv("data/amplicons/ASV_tax_species.sbdi-gtdb.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  rename(seqid = ASV_ID) %>% rename_with(tolower) %>% select(-species_exact, -confidence, -sequence)

dnakey <- read_tsv("data/amplicons/sample-key.txt", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(station = factor(station, levels = c("5","26","42","53","56"))) %>%
  mutate(layer = factor(layer, levels = c("10m","Chlmax")))
Expand code 
t <- seqtab %>%
  inner_join(asv, by = "seqid") %>%
  group_by(phylum, sample) %>%
  # Sum the abundance of each phylum within a sample
  summarise(relab = sum(relab), .groups = 'drop_last') %>%
  # Calculate the mean abundance of each phylum over the categories
  summarise(mean.relab = sum(relab), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(!is.na(phylum)) %>%
  top_n(9, mean.relab)
